rules.title: Los Angeles RSO no-fault eviction relocation assistance and Declaration of Intent to Evict
rules.requirement: For RSO units, every no-fault eviction (owner or relative occupancy, resident manager, Ellis Act demolition, conversion or removal, government order to vacate, HUD sale, residential hotel conversion, affordable housing conversion) requires paying relocation assistance and filing a Declaration of Intent to Evict with LAHD before any termination notice is served. A copy of the notice must be filed with LAHD within 3 days of service. Payment must be made available within 15 days of service of the notice, or placed in escrow within that period. Payment is per unit, split pro rata among tenants, and the higher amount applies if more than one amount applies. Reduced 'Mom and Pop' amounts apply to owner or family occupancy evictions only. The landlord may offset accumulated rent against relocation assistance, except for government-order evictions.
rules.key_value: Chart A (7/1/2026-6/30/2027), per unit: Eligible $11,000 (<3 yrs) / $14,400 (3+ yrs or low income); Qualified $23,150 / $27,400; Mom & Pop eligible $10,550, qualified $21,250. Payment within 15 days of notice. Declaration filed before notice; copy of notice to LAHD within 3 days. Amounts increase every July 1.

coverage.landlord_size_condition: Reduced relocation amount for 'Mom and Pop' owners only if the building has four or fewer rental units, the landlord owns no more than four units plus a single-family home on a separate lot in the City, has not used the provision in the prior three years, and any eligible relative owns no residential property in the City.
coverage.summary: Applies to units covered by the Rent Stabilization Ordinance.
coverage.other_conditions: Tenant status (eligible or qualified, length of tenancy, low income at or below 80% AMI) sets the amount.

rules.exemptions: No relocation assistance when evicting a resident manager to replace with another resident manager, or when hazardous conditions from a natural disaster not caused by the landlord's negligence require eviction. Rent offset is allowed except for government orders to vacate or unpermitted dwellings.

rules.title: Los Angeles JCO no-fault eviction relocation assistance and Declaration of Intent to Evict
rules.requirement: For units covered by the Just Cause Ordinance, no-fault evictions require relocation assistance and a Declaration of Intent to Evict filed with LAHD before the termination notice is served. A copy of the notice must be filed within 3 days. Payment must be made available within 15 days of the notice, or placed in escrow within that period. The same Chart A amounts as the RSO apply. A single-family dwelling owned by a natural person who owns no more than four dwelling units and a single-family home on a separate lot owes one month's rent as payment or credit. Rent offset is allowed except for government-ordered evictions.
rules.key_value: Chart A (7/1/2026-6/30/2027), per unit: Eligible $11,000 (<3 yrs) / $14,400 (3+ yrs or low income); Qualified $23,150 / $27,400; single-family dwelling owned by a natural person: one month's rent in effect when notice served. Payment within 15 days.

coverage.landlord_size_condition: The one-month's-rent amount applies where the owner is a natural person (including via a trust or controlled entity) owning no more than four dwelling units and a single-family home on a separate lot in the City.
coverage.summary: Applies to units covered by the Just Cause Ordinance.
coverage.other_conditions: Single-family dwellings subject to the JCO and owned by a natural person get the reduced one-month's-rent amount.

rules.exemptions: Rent offset is allowed except for government orders to vacate or unpermitted dwellings.

rules.title: Los Angeles Resident Protections Ordinance: relocation for demolition for new construction
rules.requirement: For Protected Units demolished for new construction within 5 years after the Declaration of Intent to Evict or Notice of Intent to Withdraw is filed, the owner must comply with RPO relocation rules. The owner must pay the highest applicable amount under state (Housing Crisis Act) and city law. Lower-income households get standardized or individualized relocation, and the RSO/JCO amounts are paid within 15 days of notice. Owners choose Option 1 (standardized payment), Option 2 (comparable replacement unit plus Chart A amounts) or Option 3 (individualized relocation). Occupant protections include a right to remain up to 6 months before construction starts, a right to return if demolition does not proceed, and a right of first refusal for some tenants. Households above low income get Chart A amounts.
rules.key_value: Option 1 Chart B (7/1/2026-6/30/2027): Extremely Low $115,480; Very Low $96,750; Low $87,450; above low income per Chart A. Penalties start at $250,000 per displaced unit. 15-day payment of RSO/JCO amounts.

coverage.summary: Applies only to Protected Units to be demolished for new construction. All RSO units are Protected Units.
coverage.other_conditions: Lower-income households are at or below 80% AMI. Protected Units include units under recorded affordability covenants, rent-controlled units, units rented by lower-income households in the past 5 years, and Ellis Act withdrawn units within 10 years.

rules.exemptions: Regular RSO or JCO relocation rules apply if the units are not Protected Units or are not occupied by a lower income tenant.
rules.effective_date_note: The bulletin says the City Council adopted the RPO on February 11, 2025 and gives that as its effective date.
rules.quoted_span: Failure to comply with the RPO may result in financial penalties starting at $250,000 per displaced unit and withholding of LAHD permit clearances.

rules.title: Los Angeles relocation assistance for demolition or conversion (LAMC 47.06 and 47.07)
rules.requirement: A landlord who demolishes a property or converts its use to condominiums, stock cooperatives, community apartment projects, hotels or commercial uses must pay relocation assistance, whether or not the property is subject to the RSO or JCO. If the City has approved a tentative parcel or tract map for a condominium conversion, the tenant may elect to relocate without receiving a termination notice. The landlord must still pay relocation assistance.

coverage.summary: Applies to demolition or conversion of rental property regardless of RSO/JCO coverage.

result.doc_summary: Official LAHD relocation assistance bulletins (rev. July 1, 2026) describing relocation assistance, Declaration of Intent to Evict filing and notice-copy requirements for no-fault evictions under the Los Angeles RSO and JCO. They include Chart A amounts for 2026-27, payment timing and escrow rules, administrative fees, and the Resident Protections Ordinance relocation options and Chart B payments for demolition for new construction. No other rule categories are addressed.
